It was an enormous gathering if five people were present from Ilidza, and in Bosnia and Herzegovina there are 109 municipalities, including the town of Sarajevo, plus guests, plus many other municipalities that have over 200.000 inhabitants, it would mean that this was a gathering of more than 500 people, based on what I know. So all the elements indicate that there had to have been at least that many, if not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Even though the drafters of this paper meant it to be strictly confidential, would you agree that it was not treated as a confidential document and that it was simply disseminated and circulated if it could be of use to anyone, and that it was not treated as confidential material anywhere?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, it was not, because "Slobodna Bosna," the publication, would publish this document immediately right before the war in its entirety. And I'm not ruling out the possibility that we could find that issue somewhere in archives or somewhere with one of our people, but I remember very well that "Slobodna Bosna" published this instruction in its entirety. And I said that to the investigators right away during the first interview, and they agreed with me. It's just a question of when this was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do we have time for one more question before we finish? This is -- now, can we look at document 65 ter 990, and we should have a translation of that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was published in public on the 11th of January, 1992, before the war. And in the second paragraph here, it states: "The new Serbian Assembly will at first act in a preventive-political manner, and in the case of recognising the independence of our republic by the European Community, it will begin to act legitimately, legally." This newspaper announces the formation of the Serbian municipality of Ilidza, and in this decision, P2408, it says that you continue to work in your joint organs. And the journalists here interpret that as being a purely declarative matter, as a mere political declaration, and that the municipality would begin to function if the circumstances allow; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as the Municipal Assembly was established, we held a press conference. And I think this is a text from "Oslobodjenje," which was not favourable for our side, and journalists always add something of their own. But one thing is correct, however. I, as the president of the SDS, and I'm sure this is something that was done by Mr. Radovan Knezevic, who was the president of the Executive Board, together with Mahmutovic, who was the president of the municipality, all of us together, with coffee, explained what this was all about. The Muslim leadership, the functionaries in the municipality, didn't have anything against this because they already had that from a while before, and we continued to work together until the last day, until the last work day in the municipality of Ilidza. That day was the 3rd of April, 1992. And precisely at 1330 hours, at the invitation of the president of the municipality and the president of the SDA party, Mr. Mahmutovic, drank coffee with him, during which Mr. Momcilo Ceklic, the secretary of the municipality was present, as well as the vice-president of the Executive Board, Mr. Nurija Omerbasic. This means two Serbs and two Muslims. And we congratulated the Muslims, the Bajram holiday that was going to take place the next day. I would like to emphasise that we worked in a very collegial manner with our Muslim and Croat colleagues; that as people, we got on well together, we understood each other. But the difficulties would always come from outside, from the top of the Muslim leadership, or from extremists and fundamentalists from some local communes where the Muslim population was in a majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to read just one more sentence. It states here in the middle column: "In addition to that, it was established that planned migrations into certain local communes, especially of Muslims from Sandzak, largely changed the ethnic make-up of the population to the detriment of the Serbs." My question, Mr. Prstojevic: Is this proof that there was no secrecy in your political organisation in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, did you say this is an article in "Oslobodjenje"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it may have been published in "Oslobodjenje," but that's not the most important thing there. However, it is quite true that immediately after the establishment --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that if you were to look at the entire page, you would see that it is "Javnost," and the news was carried in "Oslobodjenje" as well. I think we have it somewhere.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can check that. I can check that in my own documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We see "Javnost" in the upper left part. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, has the previous document, dealing with Variants A and B, been admitted? It's 65 ter 219.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There are other documents similar in topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, there are different copies of that that have been distributed, and a number of them -- at least a couple of them are in evidence already. This one, I couldn't say off-hand. I will check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Karadzic, you are not tendering that document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am convinced that the identical text does exist. I don't know whether it is the same, in terms of the layout, the design, but I am sure that the Prosecution has already tendered the identical text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn for today, and we resume tomorrow at 9.00. At that time, Mr. Prstojevic, could you try to be simple in answering the questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 18th day of March, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.36 p.m.,
